scripts.//test:llm: NOT a duplicate of `test`, and the tests it SELECTS are chosen by the script NAME, not by the command line: npm exports it as npm_lifecycle_event to every child, which realModelTestsEnabled() in tests/lib/featureTest.ts reads. `MAGENTRA_LLM_TESTS=1` in front of it is sh syntax and would not work under cmd.exe on Windows. SUBTRACTIVE like test:ui since 2026-09-21 — a test:llm run executes the `llm` kind ALONE. It was additive until then, and the measurement that changed it is in decisions/0013. This is the ONE test script whose command differs, and only by its reporters: `spec` keeps the ordinary output and llmUsageReporter.mjs adds the run's token total, which cannot be assembled anywhere else because node --test gives every FILE its own process. The opt-in is still the script NAME, so MAGENTRA_LLM_TESTS=1 node --test ... still runs the same tests — it just prints no total. See decisions/0009 and 0013.
scripts.//test:ui: NOT a duplicate of `test` either, and for the same reason as test:llm: the opt-in signal is the script NAME, read by realUiTestsEnabled() in tests/lib/featureTest.ts. SUBTRACTIVE — a test:ui run executes the `ui` kind ALONE, because the 50 ui tests were 59% of the suite's wall clock for 9% of its tests. Asking for this AND test:llm in one run is an error, not a winner picked silently: they subtract on the same axis and together select nothing. See decisions/0011 and 0013.
scripts.//test:mac: The same shape again, and SUBTRACTIVE like test:ui: a test:mac run executes the tests whose SUBJECT is macOS and nothing else, read by osScopeRequested() in tests/lib/featureTest.ts. It implies the artifact opt-in, because building and launching the real dmg is the point of it. On a non-mac machine every selected test is withheld naming the OS it needs — never passed. See decisions/0012.
scripts.//test:windows: The Windows half of test:mac, same mechanism, same file. See decisions/0012.
scripts.//test:artifacts: Same shape as test:llm and for the same reason: the script NAME is the opt-in, read by realArtifactTestsEnabled() in tests/lib/featureTest.ts. These build a real installer and launch what it produced, which takes minutes and holds the exclusive lock. See decisions/0010.
scripts.//approve: Regenerate the approved artifacts under tests/approved/. A PERSON runs this; no test does, and no environment variable makes one. Running it only moves the bytes — the approval is the diff you then read and commit. See decisions/0015.
